summary: Yün-hua Jan (1923–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He was a research fellow at Visva-Bharati University in 1953 and served as a professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).
Zack Beer is a student in Buddhist studies and Indology. As of 2026, he is attested studying at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research and the University of California, Berkeley.

Zalman Movshevich Dymshits (1921–1990) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Moscow State University (~1945–1950), taught at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (1953–1954), and was a professor at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (1954).

Zarawar Khan works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA and PhD in archaeology at the University of Peshawar and served as Assistant Professor of Archaeology at the University of Swat (attested 2019–2022).
Zawgyi (1907–1990) studied at the University of Rangoon (~1924–1929) under Pe Maung Tin (~1925–1930) and later studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1934–1936).

Zayn Kassam works in religious studies and philosophy. At Pomona College (1995), she was department chair, Associate Dean, and John Knox McLean Professor. She also directed the Pacific Basin Institute and served as research fellow (1998) and director (2023) at the Institute of Ismaili Studies.
Zdeněk Materna (1900–1944) was an Indologist. He studied at the Faculty of Arts at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. between 1920 and 1925 under the doctoral supervision of Josef Zubatý.

Zeff Bjerken works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (ending 2001) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., later holding a post at the College of Charleston (attested 2001).
Zellig Harris (1909–1992) was a linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1928–1934). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1934–1979) and Columbia University.

Zeng Yang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yang was a research student under Toshinori Ochiai at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia under Jinhua Chen (attested 2018).
Zenjo Inoue (1911–2006) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji.

Zenkei Blanche Hartman (1926–2016) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner. She studied at the University of California and trained under Richard Baker, Mel Weitsman, and Jōshin Kasai, later serving as co-abbess of the San Francisco Zen Center (1996–2002).
Zenkei Shibayama (1894–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held academic posts at Otani University and Hanazono University (~1939–1967).
Zenno Ikuno (born 1928) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held a post at Asia University (attested 1982).

Zenno Ishigami (1929–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees at Taisho University (~1949–1956). He taught at Taisho University (professor 1971, emeritus 2000) and served as president of Shukutoku University Junior College (2002–2014).

Zennosuke Tsuji (1877–1955) was a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899) and held posts there (~1911–1938), at University of the Sacred Heart (~1948–1955), and at Rissho University (~1949–1954).

Zenryu Tsukamoto (1898–1980) studied at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities. A Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar, he worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (~1931–1961), served as Kyoto University president (1949–1961), and directed the Kyoto National Museum (1961–1972).

Zensho Kitagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Rissho University as a lecturer (attested 1976) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026), and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Zerkxis Bhandara works in religious studies and Indology. Bhandara holds a post in Religious Studies and is attested as a graduate student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2026).
Zesho Machida was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as bettō at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and was a professor emeritus at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
